title: Profile cache contains MongoDB shell literals instead of JSON
fault_primitive: Recurring Memcached publication of Mongo shell JavaScript literals under existing hotel keys

diagnosis.description: An unmanaged catalog refresh process in mongodb-reservation writes MongoDB shell literals, including ObjectId expressions, into memcached-profile hotel records. The profile reader expects JSON and cannot decode those cache values. Hotel search and recommendation requests fail during frontend response construction, while the canonical MongoDB catalog remains correct. The reservation database itself is not corrupt. Flushing the cache alone is temporary because the refresh process republishes the incompatible records.

incident_class: Abandoned operational refresh process with a serialization contract regression
symptoms: Hotel search and recommendation requests terminate with frontend HTTP handler panics and empty replies. Application pods remain Running and Ready, the persistent catalog is correct, and direct backend RPC calls can succeed. Flushing or restarting the cache restores service until the next scheduled publication.
